newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran slams Germany as "political midget" for trial.
newsitem.headline: Iran slams Germany as "political midget" for trial.

text.p: Iranian state television on Friday blasted Germany as a "political midget", questioning Tehran's extensive trade ties with Bonn after a German prosecutor accused Iran of ordering the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
"Despite economic superiority and alleged leadership of Europe, Germany is politically no more than a midget," the state-run television said in a commentary.
German prosecutors on Friday demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese, after accusing Tehran of ordering the deaths of three Kurdish opposition leaders and their translator in 1992.

"Can Germany which lacks independence and intiative, especially in its foreign policy, be considered a trustworthy top trade partner of an important and strategic country such as Iran?," the television said.
"By accusing Iran, Bonn has disregarded its national interest just to appease Tel Aviv and Washington," it added.
Iran has denied any role in the killings and protested on Thursday to Germany, its main trade partner, over the charges.
Judiciary head Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi earlier said Tehran might release documents on alleged German help in making Iraqi chemical weapons during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
Several hundred Iranians protested on Friday in front of the German embassy in Tehran, which was protected by dozens of police, journalists said.
Germany tightened export controls in 1992 after revelations that some German firms had helped Iraq develop rockets and chemical weapons.
